cause.statement: SM8 scripted the crash as "answered, then died" (exit_after_responses 2: after the smoke and the first task completion) on a one-pair trial. Both calls of that pair arrive within milliseconds; when the mock answers both before the counting thread flips the library and exits, no arrival needs the server any more, the trial reaches its horizon and closes about 0.24 s later, before the next 5 s health poll and without a pair boundary. The exit is then seen only by the closing stop (server_stopped, return code 9), no supervised restart is ever attempted, the serving-manifest check that SM8 exists to exercise is never reached, and the entry exits 0. The library change itself did happen and persisted.

fix.shim: new _shim option exit_before_response N: the process flips (when asked) and exits on RECEIVING the N-th completion request, before answering it; the count, the flip and the exit are one critical section (also for exit_after_responses), so exactly one thread flips; every flip is recorded in $EB1C_SHIM_STATE/flips.jsonl (fsync'd before the exit: marker_found, sha256 before/after, pid, t_mono_ns, t_wall_ns); hold_until_written / hold_until_received force the interleavings of the controls below
fix.test: SM8 and its control now crash with exit_before_response 2 (the pair's first call is never answered, so its arrival waits on the server and a supervised restart is REQUIRED before the trial can end). SM8 first asserts its precondition (assertFlipPrecedesTheRestart): exactly one flip, marker found, bytes before == the serving manifest's recorded digest of libeb1c-core.0.dylib, bytes after != before and == the file on disk after the run, exactly one server_down with an arrival in flight, flip t_mono_ns < server_down t_mono_ns (one monotonic clock); then its unchanged verdict (exit 1, the same lifecycle, pid 0, restart_index 1, one launch). The control asserts no flip record, the same required restart (server_down with arrivals in flight), server_restarted, no server_start_failed, two launches

observation_for_root_not_changed: A held server whose process exits after the last health poll, once every call of the last pair was answered, is recorded only by the closing stop (server_stopped with return code 9) and never as server_down. This follows protocol 5.3's 5 s poll and the EB1c boundary check at IDLE, which the horizon path (DECIDED) does not visit; no episode is affected (every call was answered before the exit) and no process is started after it, so no serving-manifest check is owed. Production is unchanged; named so root can rule whether a closing stop that finds a crash return code should be a server_down.
